# walk-payload-corpus.txt — the tracked payload differential for the guards' token walks.
#
# One row per payload. Every hook suite that owns rows reads this file through its own
# harness and runs each row whose `hook` field names its guard; block-destructive.test.sh
# reads the `block-destructive` rows (arms WALKCORPUS-*). The row format, the verdict
# classes, the placeholders, how the corpus identity is recomputed, and the procedure for
# adding rows are in README.md beside this file. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines
# are ignored.
#
#   id|hook|group|twin|gt|verdict|command
#
#   twin     the id of the same invocation with its quoting removed, or `-`
#   gt       what the real interpreter did when the row was authored: X ran the unlisted
#            script, o ran only the allowlisted one, w ran the extensionless wrapper,
#            e ran another extensionless file in the script's place (extglob, -n),
#            s ran a program fed on stdin and no script named on the line, - ran
#            nothing, ? not run
#   verdict  the guard's recorded verdict: a allowed, B refused (exit 2), W warned at a
#            rollout phase (exit 0 with a would-fire record)
#   group    `open-<class>` marks an allowed execution declared open: the row records
#            today's allow, and the change that closes it updates the verdict and drops
#            the `open-` prefix in the same commit
#
# Placeholders: @D@ is the fixture directory, in which ok.sh and ok.py are the only
# allowlisted paths; @LONGX@ @LONGN@ are 4,100 x / n; @SHORTX@ 4,000 x; @MIDX@ @MIDN@
# 1,000 x / n; @QPAD@ 2,050 pairs of empty double quotes. $NOPE7019, $VAR and $HOME are
# plain text to the guard: a PreToolUse hook sees argv unexpanded.

# --- seed 1: the Stage-5 measurement corpus for the quote-closes-early family (304 rows) ---

# --- seed 6: card #7020 — the wrapper walk's own options, and tables M-1 to M-3 of its adversarial review (139 rows) ---
# Rows for the wrapper walk's option rows (nice, stdbuf, timeout, and every wrapper's own
# options), the keyword line, and the rows of tables M-1 to M-3 of the card's adversarial
# design review, which the card's differential criterion names. Ids are WR plus a number.
# Ground truth is `?` on every row but six: no command that runs a script was executed for
# this block outside the hook suite's own hermetic copies, and the review's tables record
# what each one runs. The six are rows of wrap-prec, run at the card's Stage 7 on the
# reference host's own programs, each in a fresh sandbox holding only two marker scripts
# whose one effect is to create a sentinel elsewhere: no sentinel appeared, so `-` (WR73,
# WR75 to WR78 as written; WR71 through the host's `-C` spelling of `--chdir`, because the
# host's env reads no long option). WR72 and WR74 were not run and stay `?`. Groups: wrap-opt, wrap-optrec and wrap-xargs are what the change closes;
# wrap-near, wrap-xargs-ctl, wrap-kw-ctl and wrap-qval-ctl are must-not-flag or unchanged
# controls; wrap-env-s and wrap-qval keep the verdict they had; wrap-prec are declared
# precision improvements (an option's argument, an env operand: the program executes
# neither path); wrap-overblock and wrap-overread are declared over-blocks; wrap-declared
# are executions or shapes the walk does not reach, each declared in the readiness text.
# WR150 and WR151, an abbreviated long option with a separate value, were declared here and
# are closed by the card's iteration for its Stage 7 finding F-01 (group wrap-abbrev, below).

# --- iteration 1 on card #7019, for its Stage 7 finding F-01: a quote-led word that spells a dash flag, its quote closing inside the operand suffix (56 rows) ---
# A token whose quote closes inside the arm's operand suffix, `'-x.s'h`, is the word `-x.sh`.
# Its probe (`-x.s`) and its raw token (ending `'h`) land in no domain, so only the word's own
# value claimed it: the walk ended on it as the operand, and the operand path, which reads the
# probe and the raw token, adjudicated nothing. Its unquoted twin begins with `-`, so the raw
# view steps over it and the script behind it is adjudicated. A word whose exact value begins
# with `-` is now stepped over the same way, even when that value lands in the operand domain.
# Ids are DS plus a number. Ground truth on DS01 to DS14 and on DS62 is the Stage 7 measurement
# of the same spellings (bash 3.2.57 and zsh 5.9 as the outer shell, marker scripts): the shell
# rejects the option on DS01 to DS06 and on DS14, the unlisted script runs on DS07 to DS13, and
# the allowlisted script runs on DS62. Every other row of this block was not run, `?`.
# Groups: dash-suffix is what the change closes (DS15 to DS17 are three more spellings of the
# class); dash-suffix-twin are their unquoted twins; dash-suffix-ctl keep the verdict they had,
# because the normalizer, the probe or the raw token claims the token before the word is read;
# dash-suffix-near must stay allowed; dash-suffix-decl are two pairs this change leaves as they
# were, each quoted row weaker than its unquoted spelling by declaration — a word whose own
# value is the operand (`'+x.s'h`), and the same split suffix in an option's argument slot. Both
# are the split-suffix operand the readiness text declares open, so their twin field is `-`
# and WALKCORPUS-TWIN does not grade them; each pair is graded by its group's arm.
DS01|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS21|-|B|bash '-x.s'h @D@/na.sh
DS02|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS22|-|B|bash -n '-x.s'h @D@/na.sh
DS03|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS23|-|B|bash '--rcfile=x.s'h @D@/na.sh
DS04|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS24|-|B|zsh '-oxtrace.s'h @D@/na.sh
DS05|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS25|-|B|zsh '--emulate=sh.s'h @D@/na.sh
DS06|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS26|-|B|source '-x.s'h @D@/na.sh
DS07|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS27|X|W|python3 '-Wx.p'y @D@/na.py
DS08|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS28|X|W|python3 '-Xfoo.p'y @D@/na.py
DS09|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS29|X|W|python3 '-Wignore::x.p'y @D@/na.py
DS10|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS30|X|W|perl '-Ifoo.p'm @D@/na.pl
DS11|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS31|X|W|perl '-Ifoo.p'l @D@/na.pl
DS12|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS32|X|W|ruby '-Ifoo.r'b @D@/na.rb

DS17|block-destructive|dash-suffix|DS27|?|W|python3 "-Wx.p"y @D@/na.py

# --- iteration 1 on card #7020, for its Stage 7 finding F-01: a long option read as its parser reads it, unique prefixes included (57 rows) ---
# Every wrapper row that lists a long option belongs to a getopt_long program, and getopt_long
# takes an exact name, or any prefix that names exactly one of its long options, for that
# option. The walk matched a long option as written, so `env --split=<path>` — env's split
# string, which GNU env executes — was stepped over as an option no row lists, and a recorded
# execution became an allow. A long token is now resolved against the program's own option
# table first, and the row is asked about the option it resolves to. Ids are GL plus a number.
# Ground truth is `?` on every row: no row was run. The reference host has no GNU build of env,
# nice, stdbuf, timeout, xargs or time, and its own env, nice, stdbuf and time read no long
# option; a sudo or xargs row runs a script, which is not run behind a walk the hook in force
# does not adjudicate. What each row runs is taken from the published manuals and the
# programs' option tables. Groups: wrap-abbrev is what the change closes — the five measured
# spellings of the finding and the shortest prefix of every long option a row lists as taking
# an argument, each now read as that option; WR150 and WR151, which slice 3 declared, move into
# it in this commit. wrap-abbrev-same keep the verdict they had (a separate split string, an
# option whose argument is optional, an exact name, a numeric adjustment, and the `--output`
# GNU time's manual prints, now read as a prefix of its parser's `--output-file`).
# wrap-abbrev-prec is an option's argument shaped like a script path, reached through a prefix:
# nothing executes the path, as for wrap-prec. wrap-abbrev-exec is a prefix whose argument was
# read as the interpreter; the program runs the script directly, so the direct-execution arm's
# verdict applies. wrap-abbrev-declared is an attached command line written with a prefix,
# which now takes the full spelling's verdict (WR68). wrap-abbrev-ambig is a prefix of two or
# more options, which the program rejects and runs nothing for.
GL01|block-destructive|wrap-abbrev|-|?|W|env --split=@D@/na.sh

# --- seed 7: card #7028 — enclosure positions adjudicated by a second view (69 rows) ---
# A substitution, backticks, a process substitution or a parenthesised group is not a
# separator, so the verb inside one never started a segment and was not adjudicated. The rule
# now opens one command position after every `(` and every backtick and runs the same walk
# there. A shell interpreter or `source` finding at such a position follows a third rollout
# family, DESTRUCTIVE_022_ENCL_PHASE, which ships at `warn`, so those rows record W, not B; a
# direct execution or a non-shell interpreter there is recorded at its own arm's phase. Ids
# are EN plus a number. Ground truth is the Stage 5 design's and the independent review's
# real-shell measurement (bash 3.2 and zsh 5.9, marker scripts) for each shape class those
# records state a result for, and `?` where neither does; no row was run here, because every
# Bash call this change's author made went through the hook before this change. Groups: encl
# is what the change closes, each row allowed before it and recorded now; encl-assign is a
# substitution in an assignment value, recorded before through the direct-execution arm and
# now also by the arm that owns the interpreter, so its verdict letter does not move;
# encl-carrier is a carrier's quoted-argument exemption crossing an enclosure, one of the two
# adjacent fail-opens; encl-exec is a direct execution or a non-shell interpreter at an
# enclosure position; encl-ctl is refused by the first view before and after, the controls
# that a non-carrier head or a basename accident already reach; encl-near must stay allowed;
# encl-overmatch is text nothing executes, declared, which records now and is refused once the
# phase graduates; open-encl is an execution the second view does not reach, declared open —
# a `case` arm, `coproc`, a brace group, backticks nested through escaped backticks, quoting
# the cut does not model, an apostrophe in a nested string, and a carrier at the head of an
# unquoted substitution. Commands needing a newline (the here-document shapes) are suite arms
# only.
EN01|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo $(bash @D@/na.sh)
EN02|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo "$(bash @D@/na.sh)"
EN03|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo $(source @D@/na.sh)
EN04|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo $(. @D@/na.sh)
EN07|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|OUT="$(bash na.sh --flag)"
EN09|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo `bash @D@/na.sh`
EN10|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo "`bash @D@/na.sh`"
EN11|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|cat <(bash @D@/na.sh)
EN12|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|echo hi > >(bash @D@/na.sh)
EN13|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|(bash @D@/na.sh)
EN14|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|time (bash @D@/na.sh arg)
EN15|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|(xargs bash @D@/na.sh < /dev/null)
EN16|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|echo x | (xargs bash)
EN17|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|X="$(bash @D@/na.sh)-suffix"
EN18|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|echo "[$(bash @D@/na.sh)]"
EN19|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|echo ${X:-$(bash @D@/na.sh)}
EN20|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|echo $(bash $(echo -n) @D@/na.sh)
EN21|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|echo $(bash "$(pwd)/na.sh")
EN22|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|(X=$(date) bash @D@/na.sh)
EN23|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|echo $(env X=\) bash @D@/na.sh)
EN24|block-destructive|encl|-|X|W|$(bash @D@/na.sh)
EN26|block-destructive|encl|-|?|W|(source @D@/na.sh)
EN05|block-destructive|encl-assign|-|X|W|X=$(bash @D@/na.sh)
EN06|block-destructive|encl-assign|-|X|W|X="$(bash @D@/na.sh)"
EN08|block-destructive|encl-assign|-|X|W|for i in 1 2; do X="$(bash "@D@/na.sh" arg)"; done
EN30|block-destructive|encl-carrier|-|X|W|echo $(bash -c 'cd /tmp; bash @D@/na.sh')

# Stage 7 F-08 (sub-task #8177, #7020 iteration 2): an attached split string that carries no
# command word, then the command. GNU env prepends the split words to what follows and runs the
# command that follows, so the walk now continues past the split token and adjudicates it.
# Recorded at the fixed verdict; against the pre-fix hook of slice 3 (7301d635) these move toward
# refusal, not allow. SN09 shows an arg-taking option in the value consuming the following token.
# Ground truth ? — the reference host has no GNU env, so the split-string semantics are not run.

# Stage 7 F-09 (sub-task #8177, #7020 iteration 2): the third declared precision class — a
# dash-led token whose option name no row lists, unknown or a prefix of two or more options,
# carrying an attached script path behind a listed wrapper. The walk steps over it as a flag,
# so the command is the token that follows; the program rejects the option and runs nothing.
# Recorded at the current verdict; against the pre-fix hook of slice 3 these move from recorded
# to allowed, a precision improvement beside wrap-prec. PN03's short cluster is read letter by
# letter, so its verdict depends on the fixed fixture path, whose letter a takes the rest.
# Ground truth ? — the parsers' documented rejection, not run here.
